title: Treating thrush and bacterial vaginosis
what: This is treatment for common causes of itching and unusual discharge. The doctor takes a swab and chooses treatment.
why: For itching, burning, thick white or gray discharge, or a bad smell.
duration: the visit usually takes 15 to 20 minutes; swab results are usually ready in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: What the discharge is like and how long you have had it
If you are or could be pregnant
What medicines you took recently, especially antibiotics

prepare.title: Before the swab
prepare.text: For 1 to 2 days, do not douche or use vaginal suppositories unless your doctor prescribed them.

prepare.title: Sex
prepare.text: Usually avoid sex for 1 to 2 days before the visit.

prepare.title: Hygiene
prepare.text: The evening before, wash with warm water and no scented products.

steps: The doctor asks about your symptoms
You lie on the exam chair
The doctor looks inside with a speculum
A swab is taken with a soft brush
Treatment is prescribed: suppositories, cream, or tablets
The doctor explains how and for how many days to use it
feel: The swab is a little unpleasant but does not hurt
after: Finish the whole course, even if you feel better
You are usually advised to avoid sex during treatment
Sometimes your partner is treated too. The doctor will tell you
If it comes back, see the doctor again
red_flags: Pain low in your belly and a fever over 38°C
Sores or blisters on the skin

faq.a: It is better to see a doctor first. Similar symptoms can have different causes, and the treatment is different.
Thrush and vaginosis are usually not considered sexually transmitted infections, but sometimes the partner is treated too.

reminders.text: Gynecologist visit tomorrow. No douching or suppositories today, unless your doctor prescribed them.
